changes.before: Write totals(rows). Each row has item and quantity. Return a Map that adds quantities for identical item names. Keep first-seen item order and leave the input unchanged. Quantities are nonnegative integers.
changes.after: Add together requests for the same supply.

before: Several people can request the same supply. A grouped total combines rows with the same item name. The input is an array of objects; each object has item and quantity. Your output will be a Map, a JavaScript collection that connects keys with values. An item name is the key and its running total is the value.

Create an empty Map with new Map(). Use set(key, value) to store a value and get(key) to read it. Getting a missing key returns undefined. Map keeps the order in which distinct keys were first inserted. Updating an existing key changes its value without moving it to the end.

The ?? operator chooses its right-hand value when its left-hand value is null or undefined. For a missing item, counts.get(item) ?? 0 gives you a starting total of zero. This also preserves an existing zero. A for...of loop can then visit every request exactly once.

Map treats ordinary strings such as "constructor" as ordinary keys. This avoids the special inherited properties found on a plain object. Names are compared exactly here: "Pen" and "pen" are separate items. The requirements do not ask you to clean names, so do not silently merge them.

Create a fresh Map inside totals each time. Read each row without changing it. An empty input should produce an empty Map, and a zero-quantity request should still create its item. The checks use repeated and unusual names as well as different totals; hard-coding the displayed sample will not satisfy them.
after:
Several people may ask for the same supply. We want one total for each item.

A `Map` connects a key with a value. Here, the item name is the key and its total quantity is the value. Each input row has `item` and `quantity`.

`new Map()` makes an empty Map. `set(key, value)` saves a value, and `get(key)` reads it. A missing key gives `undefined`.

Map keeps items in the order their keys first appeared. Updating a key does not move it.

`counts.get(item) ?? 0` reads the old total, or uses zero if no total exists.

`??` uses its right-hand value only when the left is `null` or `undefined`. An existing total of zero is kept. A `for...of` loop can visit each request.

Map compares item names exactly. `"Pen"` and `"pen"` are different keys.

Names such as `"constructor"` are ordinary Map keys too. Do not change or combine names beyond what the task asks.

Create a fresh Map inside `totals`. Read each row without changing it. Add its quantity to the saved total for its item.

Return an empty Map for an empty list. A request for zero items must still create that item's entry.

project.title: A shared supply list
project.task: Complete totals(rows). Add each row's quantity to its item's Map entry. Keep first-seen item order and leave the input unchanged. Quantities are whole numbers that are zero or greater.
project.done_when: Repeated names have combined totals. Empty input, zero quantities, and unusual names work. Capitalization stays distinct and input rows stay unchanged.
